hypothesis: An active fault that steps the range-front base level drives a MIGRATING incision wave up each transverse footwall drainage. In chi space that wave is a trapped PAIR of opposite-polarity steepness steps on the same branch: an upstream steepened crest (step_max > 0) and, a short distance downstream, the wave's leading edge where the profile below the wave is still gentle relative to the unperturbed reach below it (step_min < 0 at the paired downstream cell). Single-polarity knickpoints (H65-1 raw log-ratio; H66-1 bedrock dksn) are dominated by lithologic and wash-geometry steps; requiring both polarities of one wave on the same drainage removes a whole class of single-flank mimics at no extra data cost. Paired trains corroborated across >= 3 independent drainages along a common strike mark active fault traces the given Quaternary catalogue omits.
mechanism: Kirby & Whipple (2012, J. Struct. Geol. 44, 54-75, doi:10.1016/j.jsg.2012.07.009): a base-level step across an active normal fault produces a knickpoint and elevated ksn above it. Perron & Royden (2013, ESPL 38, 570-576, doi:10.1002/esp.3302): chi puts drainages on one axis. A vertical base-level step advances upstream as a wave (Wobus et al. 2006, 'Tectonics from topography: procedures, promise, and pitfalls', GSA Special Papers 398, 55-74, doi:10.1130/2006.2398(04); Berlin & Anderson 2007, 'Modeling of knickpoint retreat on the Roan Plateau, western Colorado', J. Geophys. Res. 112, F03S06, doi:10.1029/2006JF000553): the profile steepens at the crest while the reach immediately downstream of the face remains relatively gentle, giving one positive and one negative chi-slope step, pinned to the same branch and separated by the wave width. Gailleton et al. (2019, ESurf 7, 211-230, doi:10.5194/esurf-7-211-2019) motivate reproducible segmentation; the fixed-window two-segment implementation used by the committed substrate is a declared approximation, never their method. (DOIs for the three lane-defining papers are reused from the repository's own pinned citations; the two wave references were corrected 2026-10-11 to their checked bibliographic records.)

named_non_fault_mimic: A resistant-over-weak dipping lithologic couplet can also make a paired step as the channel crosses the unit's two boundaries; it is countered by (a) the radiometric-contact-gradient mask (GeoDAWN K/Th contacts), (b) the low-radioelement high-relief core mask, (c) the >= 3-drainage along-strike alignment requirement (dipping beds do not hold one regional strike across divides at the competition scale), and (d) 40 km blockwise standardization. Other named mimics: debris-flow headcuts and fan-head trenches (partially removed by the ephemeral-wash ksn_max<10 m^0.9 mask and the playa/closed-basin floor mask), and DEM fill artefacts (removed by the raised_n pumping mask).

confound_sources: playa/closed-basin floor: raised_n >= 50 (from the DEM fill; shared definition)
basin fill: GeoDAWN radiometric Th > footprint p95 (shared substitute, IR-66-DATA-01; data/official/training_features.tif band 15 is not committed in this checkout)
conductive clay-rich alluvium: GeoDAWN K > footprint p95 (shared substitute; band 17 likewise absent)
ephemeral alluvial/desert washes: ksn_max < 10 m^0.9 (H66-1 definition)
radiometric-contact-gradient mask: 40 km blockwise z of ||grad(K)|| and ||grad(Th)| > z 1.645 (blockwise p95-ish one-sided), dilated 2 px (lithologic contacts)

low-radioelement high-relief cores: zmean 20 km relative elevation > 180 m AND rad K <= p25 AND rad Th <= p25 (bedrock cores whose steps are erodibility steps; substitute for H66's depth_to_base<p25 member, which is unavailable in this checkout)

definition: crest(i) = step_max(i)/1000  (log ksn ratio, steeper-upstream extreme; committed 500 m two-segment dz/dchi at 10 m, theta_ref 0.45, A0 1 m^2)
down(i) = sig(i)  (committed i32 band; the 100 m pixel exactly 500 m downstream of the pixel's max-|step| 10 m cell)
base_drop(i) = -step_min(down(i))/1000 when down(i) is a valid in-grid index, else NaN
pair_strength(i) = min(crest(i), base_drop(i)); NaN where either flank is missing
candidates additionally require pair_strength >= ln(1.25) = 0.22314355131420976 (both flanks show at least a 25% ksn contrast) before blockwise z-scoring
declared_parameters.e1_statistic: mean pair_strength within 3 px of withheld segment crossings on channel pixels, minus the mean of 10 random same-orientation same-length transects per component (identical kernel, pool discipline and seeds to scripts/run_lane60.py)
declared_parameters.holdout: gems57.holdout.build_holdout defaults (2 draws x 4 quadrants, mode 'all', HIDE_FRAC 0.20) scored by gems57.evaluate_holdout (VERSION gems57-pooled-hide-v2, alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, 300 m triangular kernel), per-cell dot budget = round(40000/5106385 x per-cell allowed) as in scripts/run_lane60.py
declared_parameters.budget_reason: 40,000 = the H66-1 incumbent lane emission, keeping the comparison within-lane like-for-like; it also sits in the family's measured near-optimal emission regime (37,654-44,090).

gates.G1_first_test: paired_bootstrap verdict PROCEED (component resample mean > 0 AND 95% CI lower bound > 0) on withheld catalogue segments, mode 'all'. If not PROCEED: STOP, no surface, no emission, negative run card.
gates.G1b_off_catalogue_diagnostic: the identical statistic scored on USGS SGMC faults > 300 m from the given catalogue. NON-GATING, declared in advance: H66 measured the single-limb dksn statistic on this population at -0.113 (CI excludes 0); the SGMC-off population mixes ancient/relict structures in which a transient trapped wave is not expected to persist, so H70's population-of-interest is the active-withheld catalogue population that G1 probes. The number is measured and reported, never hidden.
gates.G2_leakage_canary: every predictive feature individually: max(AUC, 1-AUC) <= 0.90 on the emission domain (pair_strength, crest_only, base_drop, ksn, drainage_area, lane_p); dist_to_visible is reported as the deliberate positive control and is NOT a lane input.
gates.G3_holdout_ablation: in the shared pooled evaluator: lane_h70 paired delta vs random_mass_control has CI95 lower bound > 0; AND lane_h70 paired delta vs the crest_only_no_pairing ablation (identical z/candidate/corridor machinery with pair_strength replaced by crest) is reported as the mechanism test (positive => pairing adds information; negative => negative mechanism result, reported either way).
gates.G4_format: gems57.validate.assert_submittable passes (finite, [0,1], EPSG:32611, 3730x3292, exact sample_submission transform, nodata none, 0 on catalogue).
